fields.title: LinkedIn job posting record
fields.description: Dataset envelope (_input / _source / _scrapedAt / recordType) on top of LinkedIn's public job posting data, plus fields parsed out of the description text. One JOB row per posting, NOTICE rows when filters removed everything and ERROR rows on failure. LinkedIn changes its markup without notice, so unlisted fields pass through rather than failing the run.

_input.title: Input
_input.description: The search query or job id that produced this record.

_source.title: Source surface
_source.description: jobs-guest-jobPosting, voyager-jobPosting when a recruiter was read, or none on NOTICE and ERROR rows.

_scrapedAt.title: Scraped at
_scrapedAt.description: UTC ISO 8601 timestamp when this record was emitted.

_error.title: Error
_error.description: Failure rows only: search_failed or detail_failed.

_notice.title: Notice
_notice.description: Explains a non-failure empty result, such as all_filtered_out.

_noticeDetail.title: Notice detail
_noticeDetail.description: What the notice means and what to change.

companyUrl.title: Company URL
companyUrl.description: The employer's LinkedIn page, tracking parameters stripped.

companySlug.title: Company slug
companySlug.description: Handle out of the company URL - the stable key to join employers on.

companyDomain.title: Company domain
companyDomain.description: The employer's own web domain, only when domain resolution was enabled. Bare domain only: no email address is guessed from it.

location.title: Location
location.description: Location as stated on the posting.

workplaceType.title: Workplace type
workplaceType.description: REMOTE, HYBRID or ONSITE, inferred from the description wording. Null when the description says nothing either way - which is common, so absence is not evidence of on-site.

employmentType.title: Employment type
employmentType.description: Full-time, Contract and so on, from LinkedIn's own criteria grid.

seniorityLevel.title: Seniority level
seniorityLevel.description: From the criteria grid. Employers fill this in loosely; 'Not Applicable' is frequent.

techStack.title: Tech stack
techStack.description: Technologies named in the description, matched as whole words against a curated list so 'R' does not match 'R&D' and 'React' is not double-counted inside 'React Native'. This is the field that makes skill-trend analysis possible.

certifications.title: Certifications & clearances
certifications.description: Credentials the posting demands - PMP, CISSP, AWS Certified, TS/SCI, security clearance and similar.

salaryMin.title: Salary minimum
salaryMin.description: Low end of the pay range, with both thousand-separator conventions handled so 'Rp 8.000.000' and '$120,000' both parse.

salaryMax.title: Salary maximum
salaryMax.description: High end of the pay range.

salaryCurrency.title: Currency
salaryCurrency.description: Currency symbol or code as written in the posting.

salaryPeriod.title: Pay period
salaryPeriod.description: per hour, per year, per month and so on. Captured separately because a bare 45,000 means very different things by period.

salarySource.title: Salary source
salarySource.description: employer-provided when LinkedIn rendered a structured pay block, parsed-from-description when it was mined out of the prose. The first is far more trustworthy.

salaryRaw.title: Salary as written
salaryRaw.description: The matched text, so you can audit the parse.

applicants.title: Applicants
applicants.description: How many people LinkedIn says applied - a direct read on how contested the role is.

postedAgo.title: Posted
postedAgo.description: LinkedIn's relative posting age, such as '2 months ago'.

postedDate.title: Posted date
postedDate.description: Absolute posting date from the search card, when LinkedIn supplied one.

description.title: Full description
description.description: The complete description as plain text, unless you turned it off.

descriptionLength.title: Description length
descriptionLength.description: Characters of description - a quick proxy for how detailed a posting is.

recruiterName.title: Recruiter
recruiterName.description: Who posted the job. Cookie-only: empty on anonymous runs.

recruiterProfileUrl.title: Recruiter profile
recruiterProfileUrl.description: Their profile link - the back channel a candidate can use instead of the application portal. Cookie-only.
